newsitem.title: USA: U.S. foreign crudes ample, refiners mark time.
newsitem.headline: U.S. foreign crudes ample, refiners mark time.

text.p: U.S. foreign crudes on ample supply in the U.S. Gulf, competed for outlets with domestic grades in thin pre weekend activity.
Refiners were seen preferring domestic light, sweet grades due to more economic prices.
"With Brent only $1.25 cents less than WTI, those domestic crudes look good," a Midwest trader said.
He noted increasing demand for light crudes, used to blend down heavier crudes from Venezuela and Mexico.
The West Texas Intermediate and Brent crude spread for Oct at $1.25 a barrel, eased from $1.40 a barrel last Friday.
A European seller who traded Oseberg into the U.S. this week for early Oct arrival was heard offering another one million barrels at Oct WTI minus five cents cif.
"It's too expensive, but some refiners will pay that kind of money because they have special requirements," a Texas traders said.
Another seller was also still heard offering Brent for the same timing at WTI minus five to 10 cents cif.
Meanwhile, two cargoes of Cusiana rumored sold at Nov WTI minus 15 to 10 cents fob yesterday was not verifiable.
In the aftermarket, Oct Brent paper traded at $22.63 for a partial lot, about 10 cents firmer.
Oct NYMEX quotes were barely changed, with trades seen at $23.83/84 a barrel.
